newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: OPTUS EXPECTED TO FALL INTO FOREIGN HANDS
The way has been cleared for telecommunications carrier, Optus, to be foreign-controlled.

The Federal Government has approved a deal by Britain's Cable and Wireless to substantially increase its stake in Optus. Last month, the British firm announced an agreement to give nearly $1 billion in cash and assets to a United Sates shareholder in Optus, Bell South, in return for its 24.5 per cent stake.
Approval means Cable and Wireless will hold at least 49 per cent of Optus, and potentially beyond 50 per cent.
The deal needed Government approval, as 24.5 per cent was the limit for a single foreign investor in Optus.
But now the Government has removed the restrictions on both Optus and Vodafone.
The Government said it was important from a competition viewpoint, that participants in telecommunications not be unnecessarily constrained by foreign investment regulation.
From now on it said, proposals would normally be approved unless judged to be contrary to the national interest.
However there is no change to Telstra's ownership restrictions, under which, at most around 12 per cent would be in foreign hands.
BODIES OF FIVE KILLED IN PLANE CRASH TO BE REMOVED
Northern Territory police expect to remove the bodies of five men from a light aircraft crash, this morning.
The four Victorian tourists and a Territory pilot died late yesterday, when their light aircraft crashed while approaching Katherine airport.
Katherine emergency services guarded the site last night, while they waited for the police disaster investigation squad to arrive from Darwin.
The bodies will be removed from the plane this morning and identified.
Bureau of Air Safety investigators are expected to arrive at the site at lunchtime.
Territory police say the Cessna 210 had been chartered to fly from Kununurra in Western Australia to Katherine.
NOEL PEARSON SAYS RECONCILIATION ACHEIVABLE WITHIN 30 YEARS
ATSIC legal adviser Noel Pearson has warned that indigenous Australians will not allow the Prime Minister's 10-point plan on native title to become law.
The plan is due to be debated in parliament later this month.
Mr Pearson said the High Court's Mabo and Wik decisions could be the basis for reconciliation between white and black Australia.
And he said full reconciliation between white and black Australia could be reached within 30 years.
THREE OFFICERS MAY FACE CHARGES OVER BLACKHAWK TRAGEDY
Three officers, none above the rank of major, may face charges over the Blackhawk helicopter tragedy which claimed the lives of 18 men.
A Commanding officer still has to decide whether to follow advice to proceed to a disciplinary hearing or to dismiss charges.
The officers have not yet been told of the charges.

The charges are believed to be over a faulty whiteboard diagram of the targets on the counter-terrorism exerise, a lack of a joint reconnaissance mission between the SAS and the fifth Aviation regiments, and over appointing an inexperienced pilot to lead the formation of six helicopters.
An army investigator had trouble collecting evidence to lay charges, as many involved chose not to answer questions, believing the junior officers are scapegoats.
No evidence from an Inquiry into the accident is admissable in any disciplinary proceedings.
An inquiry into the tradegy found it was a chain of events that caused a convergence of Blackhawk One into Blackhawk Two.
The events were successive and cumulative so that an accident was inevitable.
Many people close to the tragedy believe the three are scapegoats.
RECOVERY OPERATION CONTINUING AT THREDBO
In the Snowy Mountains, the big recovery operation is continuing at the site of the Thredbo landslide.
About 100 people are still working at the site, more than a week after the last of the 18 bodies was recovered.
A security fence is being erected around the landslide area, which is expected to be under police control for at least another two weeks.
Over the past few days, workers have been removing the last of the big concrete slabs and picking through the rubble for personal effects of those who died in the collapse of the two ski lodges.
The New South Wales Coroner has announced that a preliminary hearing of the inquest into the deaths at Thredbo will be held in Sydney next Friday.
NEW FASTER SYSTEM OF MARKETING AUSTRALIA WOOL
A new system has been developed for the faster and more cost-effective
marketing of Australian wool.
The marketing company, Aus Wool-Direct, has developed a data base which directly matches mill specifications with individual Merino brands.
It holds information on more than 50,000 Australian wool clips.
The Managing director, Dr Bruce Wicking, said the world-first system would dramatically reduce costs to the processor and woolgrower, providing both with better returns.
Dr Wicking said in the normal auction system, wool was offered in six to eight bail lots, with those lots combined together and offered to a processor.
But in the new system, Dr Wicking said larger batches of wool in processing batches would be offered to the processor.
He said this would reduce costs in the system, with the processors obtaining a better quality product.
The new data base, established over three years, is in response to demands from sectors of the industry for intelligent and logical marketing reforms.
Dr Wicking said it would allow wool growers to go directly to wool processors anywhere around the world.
STATE FUNERAL TODAY FOR FORMER DEPUTY PRIME MINISTER
The Federal Government says the Australian flag will be flown at half mast on all Commonwealth buildings today, as a mark of respect for the late Lance Barnard.
Mr Barnard, who died last week, was deputy Prime Minister between 1972 and 1974, and Defence Minister, and ALP member for the seat of Bass in Tasmania from 1954 until 1975.
He then became Australia's Ambassador to Sweden, Norway and Finland.
A state funeral will be held in Launceston this afternoon, followed by a private cremation.
Former Prime Minister, Gough Whitlam, will deliver the eulogy.
